posts.author: ShadowDragon
posts.body:
basic is on A set up the door transfer (you can do so by variable (0,1,2)
or at random (0...2).
when 0, transfer to B
when 1, transfer to C
when 2, transfer to D.
those rooms exit go to A (depends how you want to run this).
if there is a specific way, door A need random 0..2 or variable tracker.
use pages to always go back to B, C or D.
if you need to resolve B to go to C from the same door (A), than a variable
is best to use or self switches (use scriptcalls for this).
but it's best if we know the entire mechanic you are after so we can give
a better solution/answer for you.

posts.author: RanchyBoi96
posts.body:
so basically the 3 maps are "the same room" just different water levels, think ocarina of time water temple.
i was hoping that after you have stepped through door A first time, if you step through door b nothing changes... but
when the lever on map 1 is triggered it transfers player to same spot on map 2, and also toggles a switch/variable to denote you are on map 2 so if you step through door c it will transfer you back to map 2 not map 1 (as per default loop), then using this logic for map 3 after triggering 2nd lever... if that makes sense

posts.author: ShadowDragon
posts.body:
I have something like yours in a different way, but more as raising water,
so I use 1 map, and event based leveling. (see sample):
but I use it up to 10x10 tiles tops, but your game to do it multiple in smaller
portions (as I use a plugin for this to control it).
the sample above is a small testing pool I made, and it can leave you
on 1 map.
another way to keep 1 map (without duplicate) or if you want to keep it
that way, fade out (transfer player to map C, wait 30 frames and fade in).
this is in your case the cleanest by that map.
an expensive solution and need time to understand it is the use of
RITTER_MapTransformation
but for me personally, I don't like the looks,
and require multiple maps (which you already do), fade out/in is probably
cleaner in your case.
another way if you want it more dynamic (less than mine) is the use of
TileChange
or
TileControl
if you want plugin controlled. (2 free alternatives)
but without plugin => fade out and in smooth.
as I went golden sun approach, and the plugin I use can control any event
similar like the above (for moving, rotating etc) pure picture based.
but I can't share it as its custom made and bit modified to my needs.
but that's all I can help for your solution
